title: Understanding Bias in the Model
text: The bias of a model is the difference between the expected prediction of the model and the true value of the function. In this case, the true function is $$g(z)=A z^2$$ and the model is $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(z\right)=\theta z$$. What happens to the bias when the model is trained with $$x=1$$?

title: Understanding Variance in the Model
text: The variance of a model is the variability of the model prediction for different training sets. Since the model is trained with a single data point and epsilon is normally distributed with variance $${\sigma}^2$$, how does this affect the variance of the model?

title: Calculating Bias
text: Given that the model is trained with $$x=1$$, calculate the bias of the model $$f_{\theta}$$ at $$z=1$$.

title: Calculating Variance
text: Given that epsilon is normally distributed with variance $${\sigma}^2$$, calculate the variance of the model $$f_{\theta}$$ at $$z=1$$.
